import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_48/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_48/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_48/training_2.csv", index_col=0)
source3 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_48/training_3.csv", index_col=0)

# First join: Source3_48_2 and Source3_48_1 on 'playlist_id'
step1 = pd.merge(source2, source1, on="playlist_id", how="inner")

# Second join: Source3_48_0 and Source3_48_3 on 'track_id'
step2 = pd.merge(source0, source3, on="track_id", how="inner")

# Final join: join step1 and step2 on ['track_id', 'dummy', 'index_track']
# Note: step1 has columns: ['playlist_id', 'track_id', 'interaction', 'index_playlist']
# step2 has columns: ['track_id', 'dummy', 'index_track']
# We join on 'track_id' and 'dummy' and 'index_track' to get all columns for target

# But step1 does not have 'dummy' or 'index_track' columns.
# step1 has 'track_id', 'dummy' is from source0 only, so not in step1.
# step2 has 'dummy' and 'index_track'.

# So to join step1 and step2, join on 'track_id' only, then add 'dummy' and 'index_track' from step2.

# Merge step1 and step2 on 'track_id'
final = pd.merge(step1, step2, on="track_id", how="inner")

# Reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['track_id', 'dummy', 'playlist_id', 'interaction', 'index_playlist', 'index_track']

final = final[['track_id', 'dummy', 'playlist_id', 'interaction', 'index_playlist', 'index_track']]

# Save to target path
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_48/target_multisource.csv", index=False)
